Cyber Attack Disrupts French Telecommunications Firms, Ransomware Suspected

PARIS, June 20 — A major cyber attack has struck several French telecommunications firms, disrupting IT systems and hampering operations across the industry, officials said Thursday. The incident, believed to involve ransomware, began late Wednesday and was ongoing at the time of reporting.

The National Cybersecurity Agency of France (ANSSI) confirmed it was coordinating with affected companies to contain the attack. “We are working closely with industry partners to assess the scale and limit the impact,” an ANSSI spokesperson said. “This is a sophisticated incident targeting core IT infrastructure.”

Among the firms hit are TelFrance, HexaCom, and Réseau Bleu, which collectively provide services to millions of subscribers across France. Company representatives said internal communications, billing platforms, and employee management systems had been severely disrupted.

“At this moment, our teams are unable to access essential operational tools, which is affecting our ability to coordinate site maintenance and technical support,” said Fabien Morel, spokesperson for HexaCom. “We are prioritizing the restoration of our systems and supporting our staff during this challenging time.”

Workers at affected sites reported being sent home or reassigned to limited duties as digital workstations and internal networks remained offline. “We’ve been told to stay on standby. Without access to our systems, it’s impossible to carry out most of our daily tasks,” said a technician at a Réseau Bleu network center outside Lyon.

Trade unions have called for urgent measures to protect workers’ rights and ensure safety protocols are maintained during the ongoing disruption. “Staff well-being and job security must be safeguarded as companies respond to this crisis,” said Jérôme Lafitte, of the National Telecommunications Workers Union.

Authorities said investigations are underway, and no timeline for full recovery has been given. The situation remains fluid as companies and cybersecurity officials continue their response.
